title: Persist display-client credentials and lifecycle

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Display credential persistence tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/serving_control/test_display_client_access.py

verify.summary: Fresh independent T3 verification passed repository behavior and static gates but found the migration round-trip test downgraded the shared database instead of a task-owned disposable database.

Fresh reviewer evidence passed owner-boundary, token/digest consistency and non-leakage, migration metadata registration, forbidden-surface sweep, and disposable PostgreSQL proof; T3 red-verify was then completed separately.

Fresh adversarial semantic verification passed hostile migration rollback/collision, restart, reset-after-deactivation, cleanup, owner-boundary, token non-leakage and forbidden-scope checks with no material finding or operator question.
Scheduler closed TASK-041 after Attempt 2 functional PASS and required T3 semantic-pass; Attempt 1's shared-database test-isolation defect was corrected within the bounded retry.

evidence_required: display-client-access.md#postgresql-shape + #lifecycle-and-recovery RED: no owner table/lifecycle exists; GREEN: one linear migration and serving_control commands create a named kiosk with a current retrievable token_value and matching unique SHA-256 digest, preserve both plus active state across database restart, atomically replace both on reset, invalidate the old token, and make repeat deactivation safe; decisive comparison: upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade, provision/reset/deactivate and mismatch-prevention fixtures inspect persisted rows while command output contains kiosk identity/lifecycle only; artifact: focused pytest and migration output under .tasks/TASK-041-T3-FT-003-W1/.
purpose: Create the serving_control-owned display-client store and explicit provision/reset/deactivate lifecycle without also implementing authentication or any read surface.
success_outcome: Every configured kiosk has one durable current token value and matching authentication digest whose explicit lifecycle survives restart and is mutated only by serving_control.
anti_goals: Do not implement the realtime Bearer adapter, Admin page or kiosk configuration UI.
Do not print the current token from provision/reset commands or add one-time display, automatic rotation, pairing or a scheduler.
Do not store the ESP32 secret in display_clients.

forbidden_scope: Admin token read and manual kiosk handoff owned by TASK-058-T3-FT-003-W2 and TASK-059-T3-FT-003-W3
Realtime admission and serving-context state owned by other FT-003 tasks
stop_conditions: The token value and digest cannot be atomically kept in sync in the owner repository.
A foreign module must write display_clients or a second migration stream is required.
Lifecycle output cannot avoid disclosing the token.

constraints: Use face_moment, the shared SQLAlchemy Base/MetaData and the current linear Alembic head.
Generate at least 32 random bytes before URL-safe encoding and persist token_value plus its matching digest atomically.
Use only task-owned disposable rows in proof and clean them up without touching operator/default rows.
invariants: The persisted current token_value and token_hash_sha256 always match and survive database restart.
Provision/reset command output never reveals the current token; authorized retrieval belongs to the Admin read task.
verification_targets: Migration/repository proof covers current-value/digest consistency, restart persistence and explicit lifecycle transitions.
Authorization review finds no foreign write and command-output scan finds no credential or digest.
